```{r setup}
library(simttepower)
```

This is a Phase 1 stub: a small, fast-running toy example showing the
object -> engine -> summary flow end to end, not a realistic power curve
(`n_sims` here is single digits, purely to exercise the code path). A
full worked vignette, with a real replicate count and a real power curve,
is deferred to a later sub-phase once Phase 2/3 parallelism makes that
runtime acceptable for a CRAN vignette build.

## What simttepower estimates

simttepower is a companion to
[simtte](https://github.com/csetraynor/simtte). Simulation-side
parameters -- a `param` entry, a dose, a covariate distribution -- are
*truth*, baked into a scenario; they are never something an analysis
function estimates. Power here is always about a contrast or coefficient
an analysis function estimates from the simulated `events` and the labels
`power_sim()` attaches to them (`arm`, `regimen`, `dose` when declared,
and any `covariates` columns): between arms, across dose levels, or
adjusted for covariates. Estimating a nonlinear PK/PD parameter (an
`IC50`, an `EMAX`) from event data is out of scope -- bring your own
analysis function for that.

## A minimal example

Two arms of the same built-in model, varying the nonlinear-link `IC50`
parameter on the experimental arm:

```{r minimal}
comparator <- arm(label = "comparator", n = 40, model = "irm1_hazard",
  end = 24, param = list(CL = 2, V2 = 20, KA = 1, KIN = 1, KOUT = 0.5,
    IC50 = 1, IMAX = 0.9, H0 = 0.15))
experimental <- arm(label = "experimental", n = 40, model = "irm1_hazard",
  end = 24, param = list(CL = 2, V2 = 20, KA = 1, KIN = 1, KOUT = 0.5,
    IC50 = 1, IMAX = 0.9, H0 = 0.15))

design <- trial_design(
  arms = list(comparator, experimental),
  analyses = list(coxph = analysis_coxph, logrank = analysis_logrank)
)

grid <- scenario_grid(design, over = list(arm = "experimental",
  field = "param.IC50", values = c(1, 2, 4)))
grid

res <- power_sim(grid, n_sims = 5, seed = 1, progress = FALSE)
res
summary(res)
```

## A real dosing-regimen contrast

`regimen` is a label, never derived automatically from a dosing data
frame -- a loading-then-maintenance schedule has no single meaningful
numeric summary. Vary `data` (the dosing events) directly:

```{r dosing}
qw <- data.frame(ID = 1:40, time = 0, amt = 100, cmt = 1, evid = 1,
  ii = 1, addl = 23)                                    # 100, once weekly
q4w_loading <- data.frame(ID = 1:40, time = 0, amt = 400, cmt = 1,
  evid = 1, ii = 4, addl = 5)                            # 400 q4w x 6 doses

dosing_arm <- arm(label = "experimental", n = 40, model = "irm1_hazard",
  end = 24, param = list(CL = 2, V2 = 20, KA = 1, KIN = 1, KOUT = 0.5,
    IC50 = 1, IMAX = 0.9, H0 = 0.15), data = qw, regimen = "qw")

design_dosing <- trial_design(
  arms = list(comparator, dosing_arm),
  analyses = list(coxph = function(events) {
    analysis_coxph(events, formula = ~ regimen)
  })
)

grid_dosing <- scenario_grid(design_dosing, over = list(
  arm = "experimental", field = "data", values = list(qw, q4w_loading)))
grid_dosing

res_dosing <- power_sim(grid_dosing, n_sims = 5, seed = 2, progress = FALSE)
summary(res_dosing)
```

## A real covariate distribution, and a covariate-adjusted analysis

`covariates` is joined onto `events` at baseline (first row per subject
when time-varying); the same data frame both drives the hazard (via
`beta`) and is available to any analysis function's own formula:

```{r covariates}
age_young <- data.frame(ID = 1:40, time = 0, age = stats::rnorm(40, 40, 5))
age_old <- data.frame(ID = 1:40, time = 0, age = stats::rnorm(40, 65, 5))

cov_arm_comparator <- arm(label = "comparator", n = 40, model = "irm1_hazard",
  end = 24, param = list(CL = 2, V2 = 20, KA = 1, KIN = 1, KOUT = 0.5,
    IC50 = 1, IMAX = 0.9, H0 = 0.15), covariates = age_young,
  beta = c(age = 0.01))
cov_arm_experimental <- arm(label = "experimental", n = 40, model = "irm1_hazard",
  end = 24, param = list(CL = 2, V2 = 20, KA = 1, KIN = 1, KOUT = 0.5,
    IC50 = 2, IMAX = 0.9, H0 = 0.15), covariates = age_young,
  beta = c(age = 0.01))

design_cov <- trial_design(
  arms = list(cov_arm_comparator, cov_arm_experimental),
  analyses = list(coxph_adj = function(events) {
    analysis_coxph(events, formula = ~ arm + age)
  })
)

grid_cov <- scenario_grid(design_cov, over = list(arm = "experimental",
  field = "covariates", values = list(age_young, age_old)))

res_cov <- power_sim(grid_cov, n_sims = 5, seed = 3, progress = FALSE)
summary(res_cov)
```

## Interval-censored events

An analysis function is any `function(events, ...) -> named numeric`, so
an interval-censored fit on `simtte::add_interval_censoring()`'s output
needs no separate simttepower code path -- just a user-supplied analysis
function:

```{r interval-censored, eval = FALSE}
analysis_interval_coxph <- function(events, formula = ~arm) {
  fit <- survival::coxph(
    survival::Surv(sim_time_left, sim_time_right, type = "interval2") ~
      eval(formula[[2]]),
    data = events
  )
  s <- summary(fit)
  stats::setNames(s$coefficients[, "coef"], paste0("estimate_", rownames(s$coefficients)))
}
```

## A direction-aware rejection rule

By default, `power_sim()`/`summary()` reject when `p < alpha` alone. A
two-sided test that rejects in the *wrong* direction should not usually
count as a "win" -- pass `reject_direction` and a scenario `truth`:

```{r direction}
grid_truth <- scenario_grid(design, over = list(arm = "experimental",
  field = "param.IC50", values = c(1, 4)),
  truth = function(v) c(estimate_armexperimental = -0.3 * (v$IC50 - 1)))

res_truth <- power_sim(grid_truth, n_sims = 5, seed = 4,
  reject = reject_direction, progress = FALSE)
summary(res_truth)
```

## Running on multiple local workers

`power_sim(..., workers = 2)` dispatches across local worker processes
(`parallel::parLapply()` by default, or `parallel::mclapply()` on Unix
via `parallel = "fork"`) instead of running sequentially --
`power_sim(seed = s, workers = 1)` and `workers = 2` give byte-identical
`results`. Under the hood, `power_sim()` calls
`simtte::simtte_prepare_model()` (see `?simtte::simtte_prepare_model`)
once per distinct model, in this process, before any worker starts --
every worker then only ever loads that already-compiled model, never
rebuilds it. Doing this by hand looks like:

```{r parallel-manual, eval = parallel::detectCores() >= 2}
cl <- parallel::makePSOCKcluster(2)
parallel::clusterCall(cl, library, "simttepower", character.only = TRUE)
parallel::clusterCall(cl, simtte::simtte_prepare_model, model = "irm1_hazard")
res_manual <- parallel::parLapply(cl, 1:2, function(s) {
  simtte::sim_tte_ode(model = "irm1_hazard", n = 20, end = 24, delta = 2,
    seed = s, param = list(CL = 2, V2 = 20, KA = 1, KIN = 1, KOUT = 0.5,
      IC50 = 1, IMAX = 0.9, H0 = 0.15))
})
parallel::stopCluster(cl)
length(res_manual)
```

`power_sim(workers = 2)` wraps exactly this pattern (plus the RNG-stream
bookkeeping from the sections above), so the ordinary call is normally
all that is needed:

```{r parallel-power-sim, eval = parallel::detectCores() >= 2}
res_parallel <- power_sim(grid, n_sims = 20, seed = 1, progress = FALSE,
  workers = 2)
summary(res_parallel)
```

For housekeeping simtte's own compiled-model cache (e.g. after an R or
package upgrade), see `?simtte::simtte_model_cache_clear` --
simttepower keeps no cache of its own for this.
